extraction_notes.note: The four algorithm2e floats are not reported as algorithm facts by latex_facts.py, so pseudocode_steps could not be used; algorithm statements (from the caption or input line to the end of the float) and line steps were sliced by hand (confidence 0.8), which leaves the finishing step's "starts mid-sentence" warning on these four nodes.

The source disables text with '\if False ... \fi' (not \iffalse), which the preparation keeps: a duplicate copy of Algorithms 1-2 and the tail of the proof of Lemma 4.1 (equations 7, 8) survive. Duplicate algorithms were ignored; the disabled equations are emitted only because they are numbered facts, and PP3 gets zero steps since its live body is two sentences.

Lemma 4.1, Lemma 4.2 and Proposition 4.1 are stated twice (Sec. Theoretical Analysis and Appendix A), both unnumbered environments; kept the appendix copies (fuller: extra sentence, numbered equation, adjacent proofs) and hand-added the edge for \ref{lemma:main}, whose label sits on the dropped main-text copy.
algorithm or definition: the SGD update rule for module j is a one-line scheme; typed algorithm with no steps.
Empirical findings stated in prose were emitted as claims with rigor numerical; other experimental details (architectures, schedules, tables) were not extracted.
Experimental setup paragraphs, tables of accuracies/FLOPs, figure captions and the related-work survey (beyond the update-vs-backward locking scaling claim) were not extracted.

Applying Lemma \ref{lemma:main} for $t=0,...,T-1$, we obtain (observe the telescoping sum), for our non-negative loss:
\begin{align}\sum_{t=0}^T \eta_t \mathbb{E}[\Vert\nabla\mathcal{L}(\Theta_j^t)\Vert^2]& \leq  \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(\Theta^0_j)]-\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(\Theta^{T+1}_j)] +\sqrt 2G\sum_{t=0}^T\sqrt{c_j^t}\eta_t +\frac{LG}{2}\sum_{t=0}^T \eta_t^2\\
&\leq \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{L}(\Theta^0_j)] +\sqrt 2G\sum_{t=0}^T\sqrt{c_j^t}\eta_t +\frac{LG}{2}\sum_{t=0}^T \eta_t^2\\
\end{align}

Yet, $\sum \sqrt{c_j^t}\eta_t$ is convergent, as $\sum c_j^t$  and $\sum_t \eta_t^2$ are convergent, thus the right term is bounded.
